newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-Hutchison deal steals spotlight.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-Hutchison deal steals spotlight.

text.p: Hutchison Whampoa Finance Ltd's $2.0 billion multi-tranche global 144a debt offering stole the corporate bond spotlight, pushing secondary business activity to the side, players said.
The issuer, a unit of Hong Kong-based Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, set a record for the largest-ever global issue of yankee bonds by a non-U.S. firm.
The offering met with such strong investor demand the issuer increased the size of the deal twice this week.
"The deal was a blowout ... it went right out the window," said one high-grade syndicate source.

The offering included a $750 million 10-year issue at 82 basis points, $500 million 20-year issue at 99 bp, $500 million 30-year debt at 109 bp, and $250 milllion of a 40-year issue, putable in the 12th year.
Joint underwriters Goldman Sachs & Co and Merrill Lynch & Co, placed about 50 percent of the bonds in the U.S., 25 percent in Europe and 25 percent in Asia.

Among other issuers to take advantage of the favorable rate environment to finance debt was Houston-based Enron Corp, a large diversified global energy company, who sold $200 million in 12-year notes at a spread of 68 basis points.
Still more debt is on the horizon as Raytheon Co is expected to bring a $2.5 billion debt offering via Morgan Stanley as early as next week, players said.
Elsewhere, high grade secondary trading activity saw a lacklustre trading session as all eyes were focused on the assortment of new offerings hitting the market, traders said.
"Secondary trading activity has been very dull ... with the government market going up and down we're pretty much just being cast adrift," said one high-grade trader.
Spreads to U.S. Treasuries were mostly seen unchanged, traders said.
In the high-yield sector, supermarket chain, Grand Union's 12 percent debt weakened further by one point to trade at 62-1/2 bid, 63 offer, traders said.
In the broader market trading was mixed with prices edging higher then turning lower in sympathy with U.S. stocks, but players said prices ended mostly unchanged to 1/8 higher.
In the govenrment market, the benchmark U.S. 30-year bond is up 1/32 at 102-17/32 to yield 6.43 percent.
Bear Stearns Cos Inc successfully sold $250 million in five-year notes at 52 basis points over Treasuries on its own behalf, players said.
"Bear Stearns' deal went very well ... it hit the screen all sold," said one high grade sydnicate source.
Among other issues expected to come to market shortly, is Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp with a $200 million century bond offering via Goldman Sachs, dealers said.
Price talk on the issue was seen between 65-87 basis points, dealers said.
